result.title: VLM as an Editing Pilot: VLM-Steered Velocity Control for Flow-Based Image Editing
result.summary: Text-guided image editing requires realizing the requested semantic change while preserving content unrelated to the instruction. FlowEdit provides an efficient inversion-free solution, but its source-anchored coupling can become overly restrictive, causing zero-edit, where the output remains close to the source and the requested change fails to emerge. We find that source coupling directly governs the preservation--editing trade-off, while a fixed coupling schedule cannot adapt to timestep-specific editing needs. Motivated by this observation, we propose V2C-Edit, a training-free VLM-steered velocity control framework. V2C-Edit constructs complementary coupling-controlled velocities and dynamically selects among them using Instruction-Level Similarity (ILS), which evaluates whether the predicted transformation follows the editing instruction. Adaptive spatial masking further preserves regions unrelated to the edit. Experiments on MagicBrush and PIE-Bench with FLUX and Stable Diffusion 3 show that V2C-Edit consistently improves instruction alignment over FlowEdit while maintaining competitive structural preservation, and that ILS better reflects editing effectiveness than target-caption CLIP similarity. Our code is available at https://github.com/Kuanshen77/V2C-Edit.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 FlowEdit 源锚定耦合过强导致「零编辑」的问题，提出免训练框架 V2C-Edit：构造互补的耦合控制速度，用指令级相似度 ILS 逐步挑选更符合编辑指令的速度，并配合自适应空间掩码，在 MagicBrush、PIE-Bench 上以 FLUX 和 SD3 验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「VLM 逐时间步评判并择优选取候选更新、兼顾改变与保持」的机制，可供核查作为 latent 推理中候选状态筛选与维持/停止决策的线索，但论文本身面向图像编辑质量而非视觉推理。
